## Summary

Regenerate live handoff state or produce the portable handoff bundle.

## Usage

```bash
amber handoff --target <repo> [--json]
       amber handoff bundle --target <repo> [--output-dir <dir>] [--replay-scope <sessionId|runId>] [--json]
       amber handoff validate --target <repo> [--bundle-dir <dir>] [--json]
```

## Command Details

```text
Regenerate live handoff state or produce the portable handoff bundle.

Subcommands:
  (none)             Regenerate session-handoff.md from live state and validate it.
  bundle             Write README, summary, evidence, next-actions, risks, recovery commands, and manifest.
  validate           Validate a handoff bundle directory.

Options:
  --replay-scope <sessionId|runId>   Also write per-attempt replay slices (frozen admission values + replay decisions).

Examples:
  amber handoff --target path/to/repo
  amber handoff bundle --target path/to/repo
  amber handoff bundle --target path/to/repo --output-dir .amber/handoff/latest
  amber handoff bundle --target path/to/repo --replay-scope run-<sessionId>-<attemptId>
  amber handoff validate --target path/to/repo --bundle-dir .amber/handoff/latest
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, and `workflow assess` reject output directories that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. Links to other paths inside the target remain allowed. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
